h1: P Hostel Buriram — Step Out and You're at the Train Station, a Budget Stay in the City Centre
intro: Get off the train at Buriram station, wheel your bag less than a minute, and you're at the door — P Hostel Buriram has a location almost nothing else in town can match. Rooms are clean, beds are comfy, blackout curtains keep things dark, and some rooms have a balcony. Ideal for a match at Chang Arena, a race weekend, or a train trip out to Phanom Rung without paying a lot. From approx. THB 320/night, with an aggregate score of around 8.6 from real reviews.

body.html: The thing guests mention most about P Hostel Buriram is its location right next to Buriram train station. It's about 300 m, or a one-minute walk, from the platform to the door. If you're riding the Isan line down to Buriram, this is a place where you barely need onward transport — just roll your bag straight to check-in. In town you can walk to a Café Amazon in 6 minutes and the Night Bazaar in about 15.

The hostel opened around 2023, so it still feels new, and the cleanliness of the rooms and bathrooms is what guests agree on most. Comfortable beds, good blackout curtains, quiet, easy to sleep. Some rooms have a small balcony to step out for some air. It's a simple, no-frills place rather than a fancy one, but it delivers cleanliness and value at a few-hundred-baht price, which is exactly what hostel guests are after.
"Got off the train and was there in a couple of minutes. The room was spotless, the bed was comfy, and there's free water, tea, coffee and snacks downstairs — great for the price."

Facilities cover the essentials well — free Wi-Fi, free parking, luggage storage and bicycle rental. Downstairs there's a self-serve corner with free water, tea, coffee and a few snacks. It suits budget travellers, backpackers and anyone in town for a short errand. There's no pool and no full breakfast service, which is normal at this level.

One thing to know before booking is the front-desk hours. Reception is open during the day and into the evening only (roughly 12:00–17:00), and a few reviews mention arriving outside those hours and finding no staff on site. If your train or flight lands very late or very early, message the hostel ahead with your arrival time so they can arrange to meet you or explain how to get in. The other recurring niggle is Wi-Fi — the signal isn't strong in every room, so if you need to work online seriously, plan accordingly.

For sightseeing, P Hostel suits people exploring the town and arriving by train more than those focused on the Chang stadium events. Chang Arena and the Chang International Circuit are about 5 km away, so figure on a 10–15 minute ride. City-centre rooms fill up fast on big match or race weekends, so book ahead. If you're heading to Phanom Rung or Prasat Mueang Tam, using this as a city base and driving out works well too.

The verdict from real reviews: P Hostel Buriram is a clean, great-value stay for anyone who just wants a good bed near the station in the heart of town. Don't expect hotel-level service, but if you can live with the front-desk hours and Wi-Fi that isn't strong everywhere, it's a very sensible pick on a few-hundred-baht budget.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — P Hostel Buriram

faq.q: Where is P Hostel Buriram, and how far is the train station?
faq.a: It's at 188/78 Na Sathani Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Buriram, right beside Buriram train station — about a 1-minute walk (around 300 m). It's a 6-minute walk to a Café Amazon and about 15 minutes to the Night Bazaar. Chang Arena is roughly 5 km away.

faq.q: How much does P Hostel Buriram cost, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start at approx. THB 320/night for a standard single. There are double rooms and family rooms too. Prices rise on big match or race weekends, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is P Hostel Buriram best for?
faq.a: It's great for rail travellers, backpackers and budget travellers who want a clean, central stay for a few hundred baht. If you're here mainly for football or racing at the Chang stadiums, a stay around Chang Arena may be closer to the action.

faq.q: Can I check in late, and how's the Wi-Fi?
faq.a: Reception is open day to evening (roughly 12:00–17:00). For arrivals outside those hours, message the hostel ahead so they can meet you or explain entry. Wi-Fi is free but weak in some rooms, so bring mobile data if you need to work online.

faq.q: How do I get to Chang Arena from here?
faq.a: Chang Arena and the Chang Circuit are about 5 km away, a 10–15 minute drive. Grab and motorbike taxis are available. On big match or race days traffic is heavy, so allow extra travel time.
